units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Neon sign. "Now serving Tom and Jerry."

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Do they mean the cartoon?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: No. It's a holiday drink. A hot, dairy-rich, eggnog-style punch with plenty of liquor, with origins more than two centuries old.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This place serves it from a big batter bowl behind the bar, in brown ceramic mugs.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: At lunch?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's Chicago and it's winter. I'll let you decide.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, tell me about the pub.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's been here since 1935. It's called Miller's, but the owners aren't Millers.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Three brothers, Pete, Nick and Jimmy Gallios, bought it from the original Millers in 1950, and a fourth brother joined in 1953.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They kept the name because they couldn't afford a new sign.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's the best business decision I've heard all day.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The original site was on nearby Adams Street.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a parking garage now, and the current building used to hold two other Gallios restaurants.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So they moved a pub twenty feet and called it history.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not quite. But close. The walls are covered in photos of the brothers and of celebrity visitors, especially sports figures.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Performers from the Palmer House hotel's Empire Room often ended their nights here.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Famous people eating ribs at midnight.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Canadian baby back ribs, served by the slab or the slab and a half.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the pub is typically open very late, until four in the morning.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: At that hour I want pizza.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Different walk. This lunch stop ends the first piece.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause the walk, and the second piece is the evening.
